ITINERARY IDEAS · TRAVEL GUIDE

Two weeks in Vietnam: a considered north-to-south route

An adaptable 14-day travel rhythm designed to balance headline highlights with time to actually enjoy them.

7
Seven Travel Editorial TeamOctober 10, 2026 · 7 min read
THE JOURNAL

A better way to see Vietnam.

Explore at your pace with thoughtful local guidance.

Plan with confidence ↗
← More in Itinerary Ideas

Fourteen days give you a wonderful introduction to Vietnam, but every transfer has a cost in time and energy. The secret is choosing a manageable number of stops rather than trying to fit every destination into one holiday.

Days 1–4: Hanoi and the northern landscapes

Begin with Hanoi’s culture and food, then dedicate time to a scenic excursion such as a bay cruise or Ninh Binh. If you want to enjoy both, consider how much time you are comfortable spending in transit.

Days 5–9: Central Vietnam

Continue to Hue for imperial heritage, then travel toward Hoi An via Da Nang. This section rewards a relaxed pace and offers a rich mix of history, local cuisine and town life.

Days 10–14: Ho Chi Minh City and the south

Finish with the energy of Ho Chi Minh City, then choose a Mekong experience or extra free time according to your interests. Check domestic flight schedules and allow realistic buffers between transfers.

✦ THE LOCAL TIP

Seven Travel tip: A private itinerary should reflect your preferred pace, not simply include the maximum number of places possible.
